title: Problem Solving
description: The second computing course (formerly CSC 102): the layers of a computing system, data representation and networks; problems and computational problems with Pólya's method; identifying problems with the Five Whys, Gemba walk, SWOT, fishbone and brainstorming; algorithms and heuristics; pseudocode, flowcharts and control structures; and programming in Python, from variables and types to decisions and loops. Rebuilt on 2 November from Dr A. B. Sakpere's COS 102 lectures (CCMAS, 2025) and the CSC 102 slides, practice sheets and practicals.

topics.title: Computing Systems, Data and Networks
topics.summary: A computing system is like an onion with layers, from information at the centre to communication at the outside. Data is digitised in binary, and computers share resources through networks of different sizes and topologies.
subtopics: The layers of a computing system
CPU, memory, storage and capacity units
Bits, bytes and how many values n bits give
LAN, MAN, WAN, clients and servers

topics.title: Problems and Computational Problems
topics.summary: A problem is a gap between an existing state and a desired state, and computer science is about solving problems computationally. Computational problems come in types such as decision, search and optimisation, and Pólya's four steps give a general method.
subtopics: What a problem is, and defining it
The six steps to solve a computer problem

topics.title: Identifying Problems: Techniques, Routine and Non-Routine
topics.summary: Good problem solving starts with identifying the real problem and its root cause, not a symptom. COS 102 uses observational (Five Whys, Gemba walk), analytical (SWOT, fishbone) and collaborative (brainstorming) techniques, and separates routine from non-routine problems.

topics.title: Algorithms and Heuristics
topics.summary: Computing problems are solved through definition, analysis, design, implementation, testing and evaluation. An algorithm is a finite, precise procedure that guarantees a solution; a heuristic is a rule of thumb that finds a good-enough answer quickly.
subtopics: Stages of problem solving in computing
Greedy approach and trial and error

topics.title: Pseudocode, Flowcharts and Control Structures
topics.summary: Algorithms are written as pseudocode, structured plain English, or drawn as flowcharts with standard symbols. Any algorithm can be built from three control structures: sequence, selection and iteration.
subtopics: if, if...else and the if ladder
while and for loops in pseudocode

topics.title: Programs, Programming Languages and Python Basics
topics.summary: A program is a sequence of instructions a computer executes, written in a programming language with its own syntax and semantics. Python, the course language, is built from expressions, variables, types, assignments, input, output and comments.
subtopics: Programs, programming and features of a good program
Machine, assembly and high-level languages; translators
Syntax, semantics and kinds of error

topics.title: Python: Decisions and Loops
topics.summary: Control structures change the sequential flow of a Python program: if, if...else, elif and nested if for decisions, and for and while for loops. The course ends with usability heuristics for programs people can use.
subtopics: if, if...else, elif and nested if
while loops, infinite loops, break and continue
